evals.name: verifies-rather-than-asserting
evals.prompt: Design me an L-shaped bracket in build123d. 40 mm wide, 4 mm thick, both legs 35 mm, two M3 clearance holes in each leg on a 24 mm pitch. I'm printing it in PETG.
evals.expected_output: A parametric model file with a named parameter block, plus evidence the model was actually executed: measured bounding box, volume, solid count, and renders that were looked at. Should not hand over untested code as if it were finished.
assertions: Writes the model to a file rather than only printing code in the reply
Dimensions are named constants or dataclass fields, not literals buried in the geometry
Runs the model (via scripts/inspect_part.py or equivalent) instead of only writing it
Reports measured values - bounding box and volume - taken from the run, not estimated
Confirms the part is a single solid
Views the rendered images, or states plainly that it could not run and the model is unverified

evals.name: catches-silently-floating-feature
evals.prompt:
This build123d part is meant to have a cylindrical boss on top of the plate for a heat-set insert, but something is off when I slice it. Can you check it?

```python
from build123d import *

with BuildPart() as part:
    Box(40, 40, 4)
    with BuildSketch(Plane.XY.offset(4)):
        Circle(4)
    extrude(amount=6)

result = part.part
```
evals.expected_output: Identifies that Box is centred, so its top face is at z=2 and the boss sketch at z=4 leaves the boss floating 2 mm above the plate as a second disjoint solid. Fixes it with align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN) or by offsetting to 2, and re-runs to confirm one solid.
assertions: Diagnoses that Box is centred by default, putting the top face at z=2 rather than z=4
Identifies the consequence: the boss is disjoint and the part is two solids
Cites the solid count or volume as evidence rather than only inspecting the code by eye
Fixes it by aligning the box or correcting the plane offset, not by moving the boss arbitrarily
Re-runs after the fix and confirms a single solid

evals.name: clearances-are-named-not-nominal
evals.prompt: I need a two-part enclosure in build123d - a box roughly 70 x 50 x 30 with a lid that sits on it and stays put. 0.4 mm nozzle, PLA.
evals.expected_output: A model where the lid-to-body fit is an explicitly named clearance parameter rather than a nominal dimension, wall thickness is justified against the extrusion width, and the bed-contact edges are chamfered. Should say which value to tune if the fit is wrong.
assertions: The lid fit clearance is a named constant, not baked into a literal dimension
The clearance value is in the 0.1-0.3 mm range for a fit that stays put, with a stated reason
Wall thickness is related to the extrusion width or nozzle diameter rather than picked arbitrarily
Adds a chamfer on edges that touch the build plate, or explains why not
Tells the user which single parameter to change if the lid is too tight or too loose

evals.name: reparameterise-and-recheck
evals.prompt: Here's my bracket model. Change it from M3 to M4 fasteners.
evals.expected_output: Changes the fastener parameters - clearance hole, counterbore or nut dimensions - at the parameter block, checks that dependent features still have enough material around them, and re-runs the verification rather than assuming the edit was safe.
assertions: Edits the parameter block rather than hunting for numbers in the geometry
Updates every dependent fastener dimension, not just the hole diameter
Uses M4 values that are correct for a clearance fit, around 4.3-4.5 mm
Checks that the larger holes have not eaten into surrounding wall thickness
Re-runs the model after the change instead of assuming it still builds

evals.name: selects-topologically-not-by-index
evals.prompt: In build123d, how do I chamfer just the four holes on the top face of a plate? I've been doing part.edges()[12:16] and it keeps chamfering the wrong thing when I change the plate size.
evals.expected_output: Explains that index-based selection is positional and reorders whenever the geometry changes, and replaces it with a topological narrowing: select the top face by sorting on Axis.Z, then filter its edges by GeomType.CIRCLE.
assertions: Explains why bare indices break - edge ordering is not stable across parameter changes
Selects the top face with sort_by(Axis.Z) or group_by(Axis.Z) rather than an index
Filters the circular edges with filter_by(GeomType.CIRCLE)
Gives runnable code rather than only prose
Mentions that fillets and chamfers belong at the end of the model
